note: Fifty-seven measured regions over twenty-nine of thirty-six pages, all accounted: thirty-two printed tables, fourteen figures, eleven refusals. Families: bar 9, line 2, flowchart-or-schematic 2, composite-panel 1, plus 32 table-grid. The paper is table-heavy because it prints the same five-name rank table four times and six appendix grids of raw coach data. Every table is booktabs - top rule, rule under the header, bottom rule, no verticals - and only five carry zebra shading. Seven chart plates are one Excel 3D column chart exported as a bitmap inside a vector frame, which is why seven regions are refused as plot bodies. Traps worth carrying: Tables 2, 3 and 4 share one caption text, two unrelated tables are both numbered 15, Figure 6's artwork says field hockey under a basketball caption and Figure 7 the reverse, p23 cites Figure 9 for what is Figure 10, five tables were measured only as a header band because their interiors carry no rules, and the p17 comment set prints no header row at all while the schema floors header_rows at one. rules: Fifty-seven measured regions over thirty-six pages account exactly: thirty-two printed tables, fourteen figures, eleven refusals, nothing left over. The tables dominate because the paper prints four identical copies of its five-name rank table (p1, p10 twice, p27, p30) and six appendix grids of raw coach data [place.doc_order].

Every table in the paper uses the same rule style: a top rule, a rule under the header and a bottom rule, with no vertical rules and no outer box anywhere - `booktabs` on all thirty-two rows. Zebra shading is used on only five of them: Table 7 on p12, Table 8 on p14, Table 12 on p19, Table 13 on p20 and the ranks comparison Table 15 on p22 [table.rule_style].

The paper numbers three different criteria matrices Table 2, Table 3 and Table 4 with the SAME caption, 'Pairwise comparison matrix of hierarchyⅡ-Ⅲ', and numbers two unrelated tables Table 15 six pages apart. Captions are quoted verbatim and the duplicate numbers are called out in the row notes rather than repaired [caption.verbatim].

Five tables are measured only as a header band, because a grid whose interior carries no rules cannot be separated from the text above it: Table 4 on p8, Table 8 on p14, and the header strips of Table 7 on p12 and Table 12 on p19. The row records the measured band and states in its note that the grid below it is unruled and unmeasured [table.rows].

Where one printed table was measured as two regions - the p12 and p19 header strips and their bodies - the table is counted once on the larger region and the strip is refused as `fragment-of-other`; the same rule refuses the seven bitmap plot bodies that sit inside the vector regions of the Excel charts [table.rule_style].

Seven of the chart plates are an Excel 3D column chart pasted as a bitmap inside a vector frame that carries the title and the axis text: Figure 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 13. Each is one chart and one row, with `three_d` perspective-bars, and the nested raster is refused rather than counted [geometry.three_d].

The chart families are not uniform across the paper even where the subject repeats: the three Grey Correlation score plates are vertical bars, the two time-horizon plates on p24 are flat 2D MATLAB columns with annotation boxes, the two comparison plates on p22 and p25 are line charts, and the Honor Roll page is a decorated poster with three tables inside it [geometry.family].

Two plates contradict their own captions. Figure 6 is captioned 'Scores of top 15 basketball coaches' while its artwork is titled field hockey and carries field-hockey coach names; Figure 7 is captioned field hockey while its artwork is titled football and duplicates the chart printed under it. Both are recorded as printed, with the contradiction in the note [caption.verbatim].

The p23 sentence 'the difference between ranks considering coaching start time or not is shown in Figure 9' misnumbers the figure it means - the subject belongs to Figure 10 on the next page. The row records the second citation as a trailing sentence on the p22 Figure 9 row rather than inventing a citation for Figure 10 [mention.trail_sentence].

Four copies of the five-name rank table (p1, p10 twice, p27, p30) print no caption and no number, as do the p4 symbols table, the p17 comment set and the three-row coach tables: their `caption_verbatim` is empty and `caption_source` is none, with the lead-in sentence recorded in the mention block instead [caption.numbering].

The appendix grids carry their appendix list item as the caption - '1. Original data of college basketball coaches' and so on - with `numbering` none, because the item number is not a table number. Four of those grids continue across a page break, where the header row is reprinted: the first fragment gets the title, the continuation gets `continued` true and an empty caption [table.continued].

The comment set on p17 prints two rows and five level columns with NO header row, and the schema floors `header_rows` at one, so the row records 1 and says so in its note rather than leaving the block unexplained [table.header_rows].
